newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, blue chips lead.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, blue chips lead.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher led by a rebound in blue chips which saw renewed buying by foreign institutions, dealers said.
"Yesterday's fall has provided buying opportunity for funds though interest was selective," said an institutional dealer. "But secondary stocks were falling back on profit-taking."
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 11.86 points or 0.97 percent to 1,232.49.
The small-cap Second Board index closed 2.33 points higher at 608.37, after hitting an intraday high of 614.06.
Malayan Banking, which fell 75 cents on Tuesday, rose 50 cents to 26.75 ringgit. The bank said on Wednesday it will release its half year results on Saturday.
Another major bank, Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank, jumped 70 cents to 21.30 ringgit.
Other blue chip gainers include Telekom Malaysia, which rose 30 cents to 20.40 ringgit, and United Engineers, up 50 cents to 23.00.
KL Industries continued to attract heavy volume, but the stock closed unchanged at 5.10 ringgit after trading as high as 5.30.
